p48: 48.  In 1992 the United Nations Human Rights Committee noted in its General Comment No. 20 on Article 7 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights that some States had granted amnesty in respect of acts of torture, and went on to say that “[a]mnesties are generally incompatible with the duty of States to investigate such acts; to guarantee freedom from such acts within their jurisdiction; and to ensure that they do not occur in the future. States may not deprive individuals of the right to an effective remedy, including compensation and such full rehabilitation as may be possible.”
